Ken Graham is an ML engineer at AppFolio in Nashville. Before that he was a principal ML engineer at Digital Reasoning and then Smarsh. He has a Ph.D. in condensed matter physics.

Current interests are efficient AI inference, local AI, and agent memory systems.

Since 2009 he has built NLP and ML systems for government and industry, including entity coreference, text classification, active learning, automatic speech recognition, and temporal normalization. Earlier work included Monte Carlo simulation, anomaly detection, cyber security, and behavioral profiling.

He is a co-author of [*Transformers for Machine Learning*](https://www.routledge.com/Transformers-for-Machine-Learning-A-Deep-Dive/Kamath-Graham-Emara/p/book/9780367771652) (Chapman & Hall / CRC, with Uday Kamath and Wael Emara) and [*Applied Causal Inference*](https://appliedcausalinference.github.io/aci_book/) (with Uday Kamath and Mitchell Naylor).

Code lives at [github.com/klgraham](https://github.com/klgraham).
